description: Structured / market-linked notes filed under Rule 424(b)(2). The high-signal population: estimated_value_per_1000 is the issuer markup the SEC forces onto the page, and underlyings[] + aggregate_principal aggregate into structured-note issuance by underlying (dealer hedging proxy, #110).

cross_checks.message: issue_date should be on or after pricing_date
maturity_date should be on or after final_valuation_date

aggregate_principal is taken FROM the EX-107 exhibit, not verified against it: rung 2 returns the exhibit's value before the model is asked, so the old external_equals rule compared that value to itself and passed on 25 of 25 filings (#164). Run ExtractionLadder(shadow_external=True) to ask the model anyway and record whether it agreed; the stored value is the exhibit's either way.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description: Legal issuing entity, e.g. JPMorgan Chase Financial Company LLC.

fields.name: guarantor
fields.description: Parent guarantor, e.g. JPMorgan Chase & Co.

fields.name: underlyings
fields.description: The NAME of each reference asset, exactly as the filing prints it -- for example 'Zoetis Inc.', 'Nasdaq-100 Index'. Names only: never the kind of asset. Do not add 'single_stock', 'common stock', 'index' or any other classification as a member of this list. A basket keeps every genuine name.
fields.note: The kind lives in underlying_type. Aggregated across issuers this is the dealer-hedging proxy (#110). Classification tokens leaking into the array was #167.

fields.name: underlying_type
fields.description: What KIND of reference asset the note is linked to.
fields.note: The classification that used to be appended to the underlyings array, where it inflated basket size and created a phantom bucket when grouping by underlying (#167).

fields.name: product_type
fields.description: The payoff family of the note. Choose the allowed value matching the payoff the filing describes, not merely its title wording. If none of the allowed values fits, answer 'other'.
fields.note: Genuinely needs the model -- issuers phrase it many ways.

fields.name: pricing_date
fields.description: The date the notes were priced, read from the line labelled Pricing Date or Trade Date. Report the date exactly as the filing prints it -- 'August 28, 2026' is a correct answer. Do not convert it to another format.
fields.note: Was 'ISO YYYY-MM-DD.', which asked the model to convert; it returned prose anyway and every value tripped type_mismatch. normalize.parse_date_prose does the conversion now (#166), so the model is asked only to read.

fields.name: maturity_date
fields.description: The date the note matures, read from the line labelled Maturity Date. These filings state four dates within a few lines of each other -- strike, pricing/trade, issue/settlement and maturity -- and the maturity line is often prefixed with qualifying words such as 'Unless earlier automatically redeemed,'. Return the date that follows the Maturity Date label, not the date nearest to it, and never the pricing or trade date. Maturity is the latest of the four.

fields.name: observation_dates
fields.description: Every scheduled coupon or barrier observation date the filing lists, in the order it lists them. The schedule is often irregular, so read the dates the document gives rather than assuming a regular interval.
fields.note: Variable-length per note; needs the model rather than a fixed anchor.

fields.name: aggregate_principal
fields.description: The total principal amount of this offering, in dollars.
fields.note: Resolved from the EX-107 fee exhibit at rung 2 before the model is asked (#101); the external_shadow rule records whether the model agrees when shadow_external is on (#164). Aggregates into issuance-by-underlying (#110).

fields.name: autocall_dates
fields.description: Scheduled call observation dates; often irregular.

fields.name: participation_rate
fields.description: Upside participation; can exceed 100% on leveraged notes.

fields.name: estimated_value_per_1000

required_unless.message: estimated_value_per_1000 is not yet determined on a preliminary pricing supplement -- the filing states a range (see estimated_value_low/estimated_value_high) and the point value is deferred to the final pricing supplement.

fields.description: The issuer's own estimated value of the notes, per $1,000 principal amount, as the filing states it. The filing introduces it with wording like 'our estimated value of the notes'. Report the figure the document states. If the document does not state a single figure -- a preliminary pricing supplement often gives only a range -- answer null.
fields.note: SEC-mandated disclosure; against the $1,000 issue price this is the issuer markup. Null and unflagged-as-error on a preliminary filing (#144) -- see required_unless and estimated_value_low/estimated_value_high. Worst performing field in the spec: it has returned 0.0, then 970.2 copied verbatim from a worked example in the prompt, then 950 -- the midpoint of these bounds -- on 21 of 25 filings (#163). Never put a number in this description.

fields.name: estimated_value_low
fields.description: The low end of the estimated value range, per $1,000 principal amount, when the filing states a range such as 'expected to be between $X and $Y' rather than a single figure.
fields.note: A preliminary 424B2 discloses this instead of a point value (#144); populated alongside estimated_value_high, not instead of trying estimated_value_per_1000 first.

fields.name: estimated_value_high
fields.description: High end of the preliminary estimated-value RANGE. See estimated_value_low.

fields.name: filing_stage
fields.description: Whether this is a preliminary or a final pricing supplement, from the cover-page legend.
fields.note: Deterministic from field_spec.detect_filing_stage() -- not something that needs a model guess -- but carried as a spec field too so a stored record is self-describing about which required fields it may legitimately be missing (#144).

fields.name: calculation_agent
fields.description: Entity computing payoffs, usually an issuer affiliate.
